newsitem.title: UK: Gen Accident profits down but above forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Gen Accident profits down but above forecasts.

text.p: A record fourth quarter helped insurance composite General Accident beat analyst profit forecasts for 1996, despite results falling short of last year's record levels.
Pre-tax operating profits slipped to 421 million pounds from 436 million pounds last year. Consensus forecasts were for profits of around 388 million pounds.
The dividend for the year was also ahead of expectation, rising 10.5 percent to 34.25 pence per share.

"With a record fourth quarter we have maintained an excellent operating profit in 1996, achieved despite severe weather losses increased by 30 million pounds ($48.4 million)," said General Accident's chief executive Bob Scott.
The group's strategy of focusing on underwriting skills and building the life business was clearly bearing fruit, said Scott.
"We are confident that we can continue to be successful in the competitive and fast-moving environments in which our life and general insurance businesses operate."
Operating profits were boosted 10 million pounds by revising the translation of overseas currencies to an annual average from year end basis. ($ = 0.619 British Pounds)
